messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a big CPU spike on telemetry-ingest around 09:12 UTC, coinciding with a retention compaction job and exporter batching bursts. p95 latency for the ingest API jumped from ~60ms to ~420ms.

maya: attaching the short log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T09:12:07Z INFO compactor: started compaction shard=12 retain_bytes=5GB
2026-03-18T09:12:07Z WARN exporter: batching window exceeded threshold batch_bytes=4.8MB exports=120
2026-03-18T09:12:07Z ERROR ingest: handler cpu=92% srv=telemetry-ingest latency=420ms
```

sanjay: ouch. did we get a matching spike in span volume?

maya: yes — a customer replay hit that minute and produced ~3x normal span volume. The compactor kicked in because we hit retention_threshold and did an immediate compaction pass. timing aligned perfectly.

elaine: quick q: is the exporter fanout correlated? if exporter queues are filling, it can add locking and slow the accept path. grafana shows exporter_queue_length spiking too.

nick: i pulled traces — exporter goroutine contention shows up. Looks like batching code holds a mutex while serializing many spans. Suspect batch.max_items and max_bytes settings are too aggressive for high-card spans.

dominic: short-term mitigation: reduce concurrent_compactions to 1 and bump exporter.batch_window_ms to 80ms (from 20ms) for telemetry-ingest. That should smooth spikes at a small latency cost. anyone object?

maya: let's try that on canary. I can flip those via console rollout for region-us-west-canary. We'll also add a temporary ingestor-side sampler to drop low-value spans at 50%.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by maya: rollout config telemetry-ingest { concurrent_compactions:1, exporter.batch_window_ms:80, ingress.sampler.default:0.5 } to region-us-west-canary. status: queued. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

elaine: long-term we should avoid compaction as a hard synchronous op during ingest spikes. proposal: make compaction a low-priority background job, or do incremental compaction throttled by CPU. also improve exporter batching to build batches lock-free.

nick: agreed — also consider per-customer backpressure signals upstream (reject-or-buffer) when we detect sustained high span rate. that ties into routing/quota UX: enable per-tenant soft quotas with automatic throttling rules.

sanjay: practical next steps: 1) canary rollout now (maya) 2) add quick dashboard panel for compactor.run_time and exporter.lock_wait to SLO board (elaine) 3) file a tech debt ticket for lock-free batching + compaction throttling (nick/dominic). I'll own the ticket.

maya: canary started, keeping an eye. will report after 30m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
